title: Bounded cohomology turns power torsion into rational vanishing
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $C\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], viewed in the derived category of sheaves of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $u,v\in\mathbf Z$ with $u\leq v$, and let $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. If $H^d(C)=0$ for $d\notin[u,v]$ and $\varpi_E^N H^d(C)=0$ for every $d$, then $\varpi_E^{N(v-u+2)}\operatorname{id}_C=0$ in that derived category. Consequently the image of $C$ in $D^b_c(X,E)=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is zero.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, $r=\pi^N$, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})$. By the completed-coefficient definition, $\mathcal A$ is the abelian category of modules over the completed sheaf, and $C$ belongs to its derived category through the full inclusion defining $D^b_c(X,A)$. The constant compatible sections of $A/\pi^n$ define $A\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, so $a\in A$ acts on a module sheaf morphism sectionwise by $(af)(s)=a f(s)$. Module linearity gives $(ag)f=a(gf)=g(af)$, making $\mathcal A$ $A$-linear. Apply the linear-abelian-derived-category lemma: $D(\mathcal A)$ and its shifts are $A$-linear, and localization from complexes is $A$-linear. Thus the scalar action used below is the termwise scalar action on any representative complex, and it commutes with every derived morphism.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), with the scalar-linear localization theorem cited as lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category; module scalar calculation written here

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $C$ and put $K_q=\tau_{\leq q}C$ in the ambient $D(\mathcal A)$ for $u-1\leq q\leq v$. The truncation-cohomology lemma says that $H^i(K_q)=H^i(C)$ for $i\leq q$ and is zero for $i>q$. Consequently all cohomology of $K_{u-1}$ vanishes: for $i\leq u-1$ use the assumed lower bound, and for $i>u-1$ use the truncation calculation. The map from its representing complex to the zero complex is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, so $K_{u-1}\simeq0$ by the definition of the derived category. Likewise the inclusion $K_v\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism: it is an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees $i\leq v$, and both cohomologies vanish for $i>v$. Hence $K_v\simeq C$. All these truncations are taken in $D(\mathcal A)$; no closure assertion for the integral constructible subcategory is needed.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), canonical truncation cohomology; derived.tex Tag 05RU, inversion of quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: For each $u\leq q\leq v$, the successive-truncation-triangle lemma gives a distinguished triangle $K_{q-1}\xrightarrow{i_q}K_q\xrightarrow{j_q}S_q\to K_{q-1}[1]$, where $S_q=H^q(C)[-q]$ is represented by the complex with $H^q(C)$ as its only nonzero term, in degree $q$. The assumption $rH^q(C)=0$ says that $r\operatorname{id}$ on that complex is the zero cochain map. By the scalar linearity of localization established in step 1, $r\operatorname{id}_{S_q}=0$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), successive-truncation triangle with a single cohomology object

proof.text: Induct on the integer $q$ from $u-1$ to $v$, with claim $r^{q-u+1}\operatorname{id}_{K_q}=0$. The base exponent is zero and $K_{u-1}\simeq0$ by step 2, so its identity is zero. For the successor $q\geq u$, put $s=r^{q-u}$; the induction hypothesis is $s\operatorname{id}_{K_{q-1}}=0$. Bilinearity gives $(s\operatorname{id}_{K_q})\circ i_q=i_q\circ(s\operatorname{id}_{K_{q-1}})=0$. Apply clause (i) of Hom-out-of-triangle exactness to the triangle in step 3, with $W=K_q$ and $a=s\operatorname{id}_{K_q}$. It supplies $h:S_q\to K_q$ with $s\operatorname{id}_{K_q}=h\circ j_q$. Multiply by $r$ and use bilinearity and step 3: $r^{q-u+1}\operatorname{id}_{K_q}=r(h\circ j_q)=h\circ(r\operatorname{id}_{S_q})\circ j_q=0$. This proves the successor and the induction.

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), contravariant Hom exactness; the scalar factorization and finite induction are written here

proof.text: At $q=v$, step 4 gives $r^{v-u+1}\operatorname{id}_{K_v}=0$. If $e:K_v\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ is the isomorphism of step 2, bilinearity gives $r^{v-u+1}\operatorname{id}_C=e\circ(r^{v-u+1}\operatorname{id}_{K_v})\circ e^{-1}=0$. Multiplying by $r$ yields $r^{v-u+2}\operatorname{id}_C=0$, which is exactly $\pi^{N(v-u+2)}\operatorname{id}_C=0$. Both exponents are nonnegative since $u\leq v$ and $N\geq0$. The full inclusion defining $D^b_c(X,A)$ identifies its endomorphisms of $C$ with the ambient ones, and by the integral-linearity lemma the $\mathcal O_E$-module structure of $D^b_c(X,A)$ is the restriction of the ambient one through the same constant-section map $\mathcal O_E\to\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})$ used in step 1, so this is also zero in its integral Hom $\mathcal O_E$-module.

source.place: Tag 05RU, derived category; elementary scalar calculation and the full-subcategory definition cited here

proof.text: Let $m=N(v-u+2)$. By the rationalization definition, whose $\mathcal O_E$-linear structure on $D^b_c(X,A)$ is that of the integral-linearity lemma (step 5), the identity of the rational image of $C$ is $\operatorname{id}_C\otimes1$ in $\operatorname{End}_{D^b_c(X,A)}(C)\otimes_AE$. The scalar-localization formula and the tensor balancing relation give $\operatorname{id}_C\otimes1=(\pi^m\operatorname{id}_C)\otimes\pi^{-m}=0$, using step 5; for $m=0$ the same equality uses $\pi^0=1$. An object with zero identity is a zero object: every map out of it is $f\circ\operatorname{id}=0$, and every map into it is $\operatorname{id}\circ g=0$. Its rational image is therefore isomorphic to zero, as asserted.

source.place: Definition of rationalization on Hom modules; the tensor balancing equality and zero-identity argument are written here
